body:
Both taken, placed differently, and I declined to file the second as a spec for a reason worth stating.

THE REVERT-AND-SHOW-IT-RED LINE GOES IN TASK-1303, under the existing CI row rather than as a fourth clause. You were right that it is already half-written there — "did the check verify anything / a green job / that the job's work actually ran" is this rule pointed at CI, and one line generalises it to any check: a test you have never observed fail is not yet evidence. I added the #2033 instance as the limiting case, because a test that scans 93 characters of itself makes the milder versions easier to recognise.

Worth naming what you did there: you improved on your own phrasing by noticing it was uncheckable. "Capable of failing" is a property nobody can inspect; "revert it and watch it go red" is an observation someone has to perform. That is the difference between a requirement and an aspiration, and you found it by re-reading what you had written rather than by being told.

THE VERIFICATION-BEFORE-ACCEPTANCE GUARD I RECORDED ON TASK-1303 BUT DID NOT FILE. It is good and I want it kept, but filing it would be a third discipline spec in a session where I have twice declined to queue prevention work under the operator's throughput direction — once for BUG-1475's ratchet rules, once for TASK-1304. Filing this one because it is mine and I like it would be exactly the favouritism I said I was avoiding. It is recorded where a future edit of that entry will find it.

YOUR FRAMING OF WHY MY CRITERION SURVIVED IS THE PART I WOULD KEEP. Not that it was wrong, but that the spec contained its own refutation and could still have been closed against the weaker half — because a reader takes acceptance and skips verification. I wrote both sections and only one was load-bearing.

And your footnote is the honest one: you ran the query because you doubted your own measurement, not because the process told you to. So the guard did not exist; a habit substituted for it once. That is the same asymmetry we recorded this morning — the practice held because a person was suspicious at the right moment, which is not a mechanism.

ON CRITERION 2 — agreed, and I will take your narrower fix. Amending the criterion is better than narrowing the query: O(all specs) against a 4116-row cache is genuinely fine, and "resolves to one YAML file" was aspirational precision that nobody measured rather than a requirement anyone needed. I would rather the spec say what the code does than have someone spend a round making the code match a sentence I wrote carelessly.
